extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers; policymakers and industry stakeholders interested in wartime labor, communications, and production
extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary newspaper articles covering wartime policy, labor and wage stabilization, communications orders, production planning, and military medical measures. Intended to inform the public and stakeholders about government decisions and recommended measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Man-power classification and control
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify all available man power into four groups: those in the armed forces, in war industries, in essential civilian industry (including agriculture), and those in non-essential industry; set up regional offices with the regional director having full responsibility to provide a full uniform national policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed establishment of regional offices and a committee to control distribution of manpower; organization suggestions include representatives of army, navy, Maritime Commission, agriculture, war industries, essential civilian industry, two labor reps and one 'neutral.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to halt voluntary enlistments
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary enlistments should be halted (Nelson, as reported) as part of a strategy to retain workers for war production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as part of measures to preserve production from reserves of workers; presented alongside other proposals (lengthened work week, better management, use of minority groups, reducing absenteeism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways to increase production from worker reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase production by lengthening the work week, improving management, greater use of minority groups, cutting nonessential uses of manpower, and stopping worker absenteeism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes from testimony/remarks that overtime beyond certain periods yields no sustained productivity gains; presented as alternatives to drafting more workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: War Labor Board wage/salary stabilization — Sept. 15 freeze
rubrics_metrics.description: Wages and salaries under the board's jurisdiction are virtually frozen at the Sept. 15 level; increases above that level will be granted only in exceptional cases and in accordance with the President's economic stabilization order of Oct. 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairman William H. Davis described the policy as 'pretty damn tough.' Applies to non-agricultural wages and salaries under $5,000 (with certain jurisdictional exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for approving wage/salary increases
rubrics_metrics.description: No wage/salary increases will be approved 'unless such increase is necessary to correct maladjustments or inequalities, to eliminate sub-standards of living, to correct gross inequities or to aid in the effective prosecution of the war.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will consider specific requests case-by-case; regional directors and tripartite regional boards advise; increases to influence manpower flow are not to be approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: General increases up to 15% rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The board will consider requests for general increases in straight-time rates up to 15 percent above the level prevailing on January 1, 1941, to correct maladjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a group of employees has already received increases amounting to 15 percent in average straight-time rates since Jan. 1, 1941, the board will not grant further increases as correction for maladjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of policy to groups not individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Stabilization policy is not applicable to individual workers or to employees in particular job classifications; it will be applied only to groups composed of all the employees in a bargaining unit, in a plant, a company or an industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional director may review evidence of discriminatory differences and transmit claims to the National War Labor Board if justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on approving increases to influence manpower flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The board will not approve wage increases for the purpose of influencing or directing the flow of manpower from one industry to another, or from one area to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit limitation reiterated in board statement; decisions must not be used as a tool to steer workers between sectors or regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional limits of wage/salary control
rubrics_metrics.description: The War Labor Board controls all non-agricultural wages and salaries under $5,000, except salaries of supervisory or professional employees; Treasury has jurisdiction over supervisory/professional salaries under $5,000 and all salaries over $5,000; Secretary of Agriculture has jurisdiction over farm wages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains which agencies have authority over different salary bands and categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional directors' limited authority to correct maladjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional directors will be granted authority to adjust rates to correct maladjustments only in cases arising in industries designated by the board; tripartite regional boards (public, labor, employees) will advise directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions by regional directors are subject to board's general orders and announced rules of procedure; list of designated industries to be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonuses, fees, gifts, commissions continuation conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A bonus, fee, gift, commission or trace customarily paid employees can be continued without board approval in the future provided certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fixed amount: total paid during current bonus year must not exceed total paid for like work during preceding bonus year. If percentage/incentive basis: rate and method of computation may not be changed during current bonus year. (Additional restrictions implied about yield and continuity.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Substandard of living adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage adjustments to eliminate substandards of living may be considered; the board has dealt with very few such cases and is not yet in a position to enunciate a general policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substandard cases will be handled individually and may be raised to regional director or to the National War Labor Board when evidence is presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teleprinter/telegraph infrastructure standards (FCC requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: FCC was asked to prepare standards to control present and future installations of teleprinter equipment for telegraphic users; formulate basic principles for regulating leasing of telegraphic circuits to prevent needed facilities from being used for non-essential purposes; study elimination of unnecessary circuits, facilities and offices; develop a plan for curtailment of 'S' and dead-head messages and elimination of 'free service' messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are preparatory/analytical assignments given to the FCC by the Board of War Communications to gear the industry to the war effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of War Communications order — discontinuance of non-telegraphic services
rubrics_metrics.description: Telegraph companies ordered to refuse felicitation and congratulatory messages and to discontinue all non-telegraphic services beginning December 15; included services: messenger, errand, distribution, remittance, installment payment, sale of travelers' checks, sale and acceptance of railway express packages, and similar non-telegraphic offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions made for messages addressed to American Expeditionary Forces; objections to the order will be received up to November 25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraph 'office drag' and transmission time standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'office drag' (interval between the time a message reaches the operating room and the complete transmission) must not average more than seven minutes for at least ninety-five per cent of all messages received at the office, and in no case among the ninety-five per cent may the 'drag' exceed fifteen minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the BWC order to improve efficiency and prioritize essential traffic during wartime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing time reduction for messenger-delivered business messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Present routing times for business messages to be delivered by messenger must be reduced by one third.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified as an operational efficiency target in the BWC/FCC measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority system revision for handling urgent traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: FCC authorized to develop a plan for revising the present priority system for handling governmental and non-governmental urgent essential traffic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure government-essential messages are properly prioritized over non-essential communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuance of fixed-text holiday telegram services
rubrics_metrics.description: Both telegraph companies have dropped the so-called fixed text telegrams which were offered at special rates on all holidays and for any special occasion (birthday, graduation, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These services (designated by numbers with only address, signature and number sent over the wire) are to be discontinued as part of wartime curtailment of non-essential telegraph use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export control requirements for Axis-marked goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Tightened control over export of goods marked 'Made in Japan', 'Made in Germany' or 'Made in Italy': each application for a license covering the export of Axis-marked goods must be accompanied by a statement describing the mark or label, naming the country of origin and the manufacturer, and explaining the transaction by which the applicant acquired ownership of the articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to shipments of such goods remaining in dealers' hands since Pearl Harbor; individual export license now required rather than general license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naval/ship medical preparedness measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard equipment and organizational measures for treating battle casualties: twin medical stations on ships (division of medical supplies and personnel so one remaining if one is put out of action), one-man-carry medical back-packs for battalion/company aid, light folding litters, light waterproof substitute blankets, collective litter hoists, and use of non-medical personnel to assist surgeons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to increase mobility and rapid treatment (principle of 'take the treatment to the wounded'); examples include saving time in debarking patients and designing packs for landing parties and ambulance boats.
